newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down in flood-data wait.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down in flood-data wait.

text.p: Polish shares extended Friday's fall and analysts expected another loss on Tuesday, saying it was unclear where the market would bottom out as investors waited for data on damages wrought by the current flooding.
Water currently covers thousands of square kilometeres of southern Poland and police estimate the death toll of the week-old catastrophe at 36.
"We'll reach a bottom once we find out preliminary estimates of the damages...currently no one exactly knows what happened and how much it will cost," said Pawel Demczuk, a trader at Wood & Company.
Analysts said the market could begin to recover later this week from the current drop.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.4 percent to 15,455.8 points and turnover fell 8.9 percent to 216 million zlotys ($63.8 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 81 to 14 with eight stocks flat.
Analysts said Polish players might be doing relatively more selling, in part to gather funds to get through flood damage.
Bank Slaski and copper firm KGHM were the big stocks worst hit by flood-fear, each down 10 percent, though analysts expected a KGHM correction toward its GDR.

The NFI index fell 8.6 percent, analysts said, as many of the 500 or so firms in the mass privatisation programme are based in southern Poland. Petrobank was allowed to fall 12.6 percent after going ex-dividend.

Cement firm Gorazdze, non-ferrous metals smelter Olawa, paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, engineering firm Remak and chemical firm Viscoplast joined electrode maker ZEW and industrial boilermaker Rafako as firms suspended due to floods.
